utterances.text: Witness, there's a page that's marked, and I see that you have that open before you, and you were shown this page by Defence counsel in cross-examination in the previous trial. And in respect of the entries marked 1490 and 1491, you testified that those could have been the policemen who were involved in the incident that was related to you by Mr. Borovcanin that evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This should not be broadcast because it's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. President, I didn't catch that. But you are correct, it's a document that is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In your list of documents to be used with the witness it is not marked as under seal. This is the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And therefore we should put it under seal in this trial as well. P1042.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, have a look at those entries, 1490 and 1491. And you will see there that there is a column which specifies the units these men were in. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you see there that it says they were members of the -- 1490, it says MUP, Special Brigade. And for 1491 it says Special Police Skelani. Does that reflect the information that you received about the two men, the one of which who was injured and the other who was killed, that you were told?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if you could please read the diagnosis and the description of the injury that patient 1490 sustained. And that's the entry -- his name is Rade Cuturic. Are you able to read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is that a protected name? I think the reason why this is all under seal could be that this contains some medical information which is confidential. I don't know. Please check that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm told that there's not very much that's confidential in this hospital log and there's probably no need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I only wanted to know if it is necessary to mention the name of the patient.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I can -- I don't have to mention the name. I can just refer to the entry numbers, that's fine. That's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, for patient 1490, are you able to read the description of the injury that the patient sustained?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: The rather illegible and I think that it's in Latin.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could that be enlarged, please, this part of the document in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I can assist you with that. What it says, and part of it is in Latin, is, and we see this in the English version, "burns on the palms of the hands and 2 to 4 fingers of the left-hand with," and then there's a note that the rest is illegible. Does that injury match what you learned about the injuries sustained by the policemen who joined you at the Jasen restaurant?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And for patient 1491, again the description, the diagnosis there is in Latin. It states "exitus letalis" and I can tell you that that's a Latin medical term for "deceased," as it has been translated here on the English version. Does that accord with what you learned of what had happened to the second policeman?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And for the purposes of the record, after "exitus letalis," in the B/C/S version there's no question mark. In the English version there is a question mark, but it doesn't appear in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now if we look at the birth date of patient 1490, it's recorded as 26 August 1971. This means he would have been 23 at the time. Was that the approximate age of the man who arrived at the restaurant with the bandaged hand?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And as for the time of the admission of both these patients, and it states here they were admitted on the 13th of July, 1995, is the time of their admission consistent with what you had learned had happened to this patient and when it had happened?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Well, we didn't talk about the time when the wounded patient arrived at the health centre. But I assume, since he came to the restaurant after an hour and a half or about two hours, that this is the correct entry of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to the meetings you had with Colonel Beara that same night. You had two meetings at the SDS premises and you testified about those two meetings at some length in the Popovic trial. Could you please just explain for the Chamber what it is that Colonel Beara tasked you with?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: After we left the Jasen restaurant, I went to my office, the office of my company. After some time I received a phone call. It was the Bratunac municipality. They told me to go to the SDS, or more precisely to Miroslav Deronjic's office. I was told that Colonel Beara was going to wait for me there because he had to tell me something. Should I continue or are you going to pose questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If you could just please tell us what he had tasked you to do.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I left my office and went to the SDS. There, in the secretary's office, I found two military policemen at the entrance to the office of Mr. Deronjic. I told them that I came on the invitation of Colonel Beara. They let me in. I entered. In the office I found Mr. Beara and another two officers that I did not know. I hadn't seen them up to that (redacted)

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: (redacted). I told him that we had a small SKIP excavator and two FAP kipper trucks, and I also had people who were mobilised on the work obligation to work in the utility company. He told me that everything should be set up, that we should look into what other resources we had because, during the night or in the morning, all this should go to the territory of the Milici municipality in order to bury the people who were supposed to lose their lives. He assumed that there was going to be a large number of dead. I said how come we are supposed to do this when we have so little of resources and mechanisation and just a few workmen, and we are supposed to do that in a the territory of another municipality. He told that was not my problem. He said that I should just prepare everything. So there was a bit of a quarrel after which he told me that I was free to go and await further orders. Then I left and I went home. Sometime after midnight, about 1.00 or 1.30 a.m., it was, I think, one of the military policemen who phoned me and told me to return to that office. I went there. On that occasion, Mr. Beara was alone in the office. He offered a drink, which I refused. He called the military policeman to come into the office and told that military policeman to drive me to Glogova, that was the place where we were supposed to bury the dead. When he told me that I was supposed to do that, I refused that and I said that I'm not going to go around looking for locations for burial. He said, "You have this military policeman, he'll tell you where the locations is. You just have to dig." So tomorrow, at around 9.00, we came there -- or, rather, the workmen had already assembled at the place where they would usually assemble and I told them that they had to go to up to Glogova. I arrived there, the machine arrived, and we began digging. It didn't go well. That's when I told Colonel Beara that a ULT was not supposed to dig. It was supposed to load, because it was a loader. When we began our work, it became quite obvious that it was impossible to do that. Now, I don't remember whether I did it myself or through a military policeman, but I informed Mr. Beara that his order could not be carried out. He promised an excavator. That excavator was supposed to come from the Zvornik Brigade in order to finish the job. We waited for almost half of the day. Sometime in the afternoon a huge truck came, a flat-bed truck, and the excavator was brought to Glogova. The flat-bed truck went back towards Kravica, Konjevic Polje and Zvornik, that is the place where it came from. And we continued the digging.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I'll ask you some more questions about the graves in a moment. Can you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before you continue, I would like to remind the witness not to mention his own name. It is a protected name. It shouldn't be mentioned and that part where you did it will be redacted. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could you please describe for us the location where the graves were dug?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: The military policeman drove me along the road Bratunac-Konjevic Polje. At the place where the old road turned toward Kravica, that used to be an old road that was used until the proper road was built, and that's where we turned. We drove for 100 or 150 metres. First he reversed the vehicle and parked it so that it was facing the direction of Bratunac. We left the vehicle then. He showed me, by hand, where we were supposed to dig the common or mass grave. I said yes, I understand that, and that's when we again took the vehicle and went back.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And may we have 65 ter 1031 displayed on the screen. And if the witness could be provided with a pen and perhaps the Bratunac health log can be removed from in front of the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, with the assistance of the Court Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we perhaps zero in a bit closer on that image. And if we could turn it the right way up, so 180 degrees, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the roads that are depicted on this aerial image?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could you please -- are these the roads that you just mentioned to us? Is this the site of where the graves were dug?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Interpreters kindly ask the Prosecution counsel to switch off the microphone while the witness is speaking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I said yes, maybe you didn't hear me.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please draw a circle around the area where the graves were dug.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: It's a bit unclear, looking at these houses, but I assume that it's approximately this here. That was a big one, and right next to it there was a smaller one. And then two of them were across the road, like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to offer this aerial image with the witness's markings as the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1031 marked by the witness in court shall be assigned Exhibit P2194. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: May we now have P444 shown on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise this location?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: This is the cross-roads. On one side there is the road between Sarajevo and Bratunac, and on the other side, the road leads to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And this the location where you previously testified you saw some dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Would you please mark on this photograph where it is that you saw dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Approximately here in front of this building where the gas station now is. This other building doesn't exist anymore, that used to be the agricultural co-operative in Bratunac. It's approximately here. And here -- but here you can't see the place where the church is, but it was approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did your --

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Or somewhere here. Well, it's thereabouts. But I also have to add that later on, when I sent the driver to pick up the corpses that were next to the road and those ones that I had seen, he told me that next to the school a woman was killed and a little bit further down, in a canal they found another two men. So that's as far as Konjevic Polje is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: For the purposes of the record, could you please mark the locations you have just marked with an X with the numbers 1, 2, and 3, consecutively from left to right.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, I offer this marked photograph as the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's not very clear. You should put on the record which is number 2 and number 3 because he marked it the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please -- the location that you've marked as number 2, could you please describe where that is?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: The place that I marked with number 2 -- or actually 1, 2, and 3, those are the places where I saw several corpses, five or six at a single spot. In total, there were about 10 or 15 corpses on those three places.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And the X that you've marked with a number 2, there appears to be a church nearby, was that church standing in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: No, it was built later, this church. You can't see it really well on this picture, but this, the place that I marked on this photo, it looks as if the road goes behind the church, but it goes in front of the church. Today there is a cafe here. Looking from Konjevic Polje towards Bratunac it's on the right-hand side. It's right there on the intersection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. This marked photograph will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit P444 marked by the witness in court shall be assigned Exhibit P2195. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, did you and your personnel collect these bodies and take them to Glogova, to the grave-site there?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: May we have P1045 now displayed on the screens.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, you previously testified that you saw some bodies also by the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac, and the last time you testified, you were shown an aerial image of Bratunac and you were asked to mark where it is that you saw those bodies. I'm going to show you that aerial image that you had marked. Do you see the red X on the screen?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you confirm that that is the location where you saw the dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: This is the place where I saw five or six corpses. In the evening when we were giving water to the people who were in the buses in front of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And this reference you make to the buses that were in front of the municipality, who was in those buses?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Those were people of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And did you see these buses before or after you met with Borovcanin and Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: The buses I saw the day before I met with Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: What did you do after you saw those bodies? What did you do with the bodies, if anything?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I informed the duty driver in my utility company. It was Milivoj Cetinovic. I told him to take the people who were on duty and pick up those corpses.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Were those corpses buried that day?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Where were they put?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: They remained on the truck. He collected some corpses the next day next to the school and told me that in addition to the five or six I told him to collect, that he ended up collecting more. When we started digging in Glogova, it was then that we brought a truck that was almost full of corpses from the school and buried them together with the corpses from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And did the driver or any of the personnel who collected bodies from the Vuk Karadzic school inform you of how many bodies they collected?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: The driver told me that there were far more than I instructed him to collect, but all I saw was five or six of them in the corner of the field next to the Vuk Karadzic school. However, when he went to the location, he told me that there were more corpses than I had told him to collect and that he picked up all of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did he tell you where they found the dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: In the school-yard and around the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: How long were your personnel engaged in the collection of dead bodies from the Vuk -- in and around -- sorry, around, you've said, the Vuk Karadzic school?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Two days. They were buried on the third day.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you know how many truck-loads of dead bodies were removed from the Vuk Karadzic school over those two days?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: One truck-load.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, how many days in total were your personnel involved in the collection of bodies that were taken to the Glogova grave-site?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: How many bodies would you say were collected and buried at that grave-site?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: In total, in my estimate there were between 4- and 500 people buried in the mass grave. However, my final estimate would be that the total was far greater since I wasn't at the site all the time. I went back and forth between the site and my company. Therefore, I can't tell you a specific number, but between 4- and 500 bodies were brought to the location just at those times when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The Prosecution's investigations reveal that there were 1.131 bodies that were buried at this Glogova grave-site. Does that figure surprise you?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: It's probably a credible figure because there was work at the location for five or six days. I was there for only limited periods of time, and if my assumption is that between 4- and 500 people were buried there when I was there, then the total you presented may well be a credible number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put a question to the witness for a clarification. You were asked by Ms. Hasan the following question: "Do you know how many truck-loads of dead bodies were removed from the Vuk Karadzic school over those two days?" And then you said: "One truck-load." Two questions. One truck-load every day or altogether?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One truck-load in total. As I was explaining a moment ago, there were five or six bodies for which I told the driver to collect. They spent the night on that truck and the next day he picked up some more. Later on, the truck took all of the bodies to Glogova, so there was one truck-load of corpses collected from the school compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is your estimation how many bodies were on this one truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw five or six, but the driver told me that there were more. I don't know how many exactly. Maybe twice as many. In any case, a truck full of corpses arrived in Glogova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, you previously testified that you dispatched men to collect bodies from the Kravica agricultural co-operative, what we are referring to here in this trial as the Kravica warehouse, from near the Konjevic Polje intersection and from along the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road, as well as those bodies that were collected from Bratunac itself. As regards the bodies that were collected from the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road, were there any bodies collected from the Kravica-Bratunac section -- segment of that road?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: In the course of the few days when we were in Glogova, I sent people -- the people and the truck to Konjevic Polje, and from Kravica to Konjevic Polje, where there was fighting, to collect the bodies. I didn't send them in the direction of Bratunac, and there were no corpses between Bratunac and Glogova or Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: How many dead bodies were collected from along the Kravica-Konjevic Polje road?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: A truck-load. A truck full of corpses was brought in, so between 20 and 25 on that single truck.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just a moment. Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you. At -- I can't pick up the page, but I think it's just now on line 22, 23, you have stated: "... and from Kravica to Konjevic Polje, where there was fighting, to collect the bodies." Have I quoted you correctly. Now, I want you to just clarify for me who was fighting in that location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those were the bodies of killed Muslim soldiers, that is to say, people who had arms in combat against the VRS. They were trying to break through to or along the Kravica-Konjevic Polje road, so there were some corpses which we collected there as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The figure that you mentioned of the number of bodies in the truck-load that were taken from along the Konjevic Polje-Kravica road, does that figure include the 15 or so bodies that you collected from the three locations that you just marked on the photograph that shows the cross-roads at Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you or your personnel collect any bodies from the areas that were mined or that you thought were mined?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Please tell us why not?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: The driver and people I sent to collect the roads [as interpreted] along the roads and nearby the roads were told by me not to go any further afield because the terrain was mined. I didn't want to make things worse than they were. I didn't want the things to become worse so I cautioned them not to do that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Line 22, it should be "I sent to collect the corpses."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So do I understand you correctly, were your men restricted to collecting bodies from the road itself?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes, you understood that well. I told them, "Don't stray from the road, go out by mere 2 to 3 metres and not more." We all knew that the area was mined, and this is how they did it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Aside from the locations we've just mentioned where you've collected dead bodies from, were your men assigned to collect -- to gather dead bodies from any other locations?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I didn't know of any other locations, only Kravica. Our truck from the public utility company, the FAP 13, took the corpses to the Glogova site. There were some other trucks engaged in it from Milici, Vlasenica and Zvornik as well. We didn't go to any other locations and I didn't know of any.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And we have in evidence your testimony about the collection of bodies from Kravica. Just one final question or -- yeah, just the operation, if I can call it that, of the burial of the bodies at the Glogova grave-site, was that done pursuant to the order that Beara conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, that concludes my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, now you may commence your cross-examination. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Peace unto this house and may this hearing be concluded in keeping with God's will and not my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to greet the witness and wish him a pleasant stay with us. If possible, I'd kindly ask him to provide answers to my questions.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to greet you, Mr. Tolimir, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. At page 60, line 20, Ms. Hasan asked you how many bodies were taken from the road between Konjevic Polje and Kravica. You said, in line 21, that there were between 20 and 25, that is to say, a truck full of corpses. My question is whether the approximate figure of 20 to 25 bodies can be put on to a single truck?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Well, I said there was a truck full of corpses and one can put between 20 and 25 corpses on one truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm content with your answer. This is precisely what I wanted to ask you. In line 18, page 61, Ms. Hasan asked you whether you collected corpses from the areas that were mined. In line 22 you said, "Yes, I told them not to collect bodies from the areas mined." Since there seems to be a bit of confusion there, can you tell us whether you indeed ordered your men not to leave the road and enter the mined areas?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I was asked whether I ordered the workers not to collect bodies from the areas that were mined, and I answered yes. I ordered them not to collect any corpses from the areas that were mined. We only collected bodies along the road and immediately adjacent to it. We didn't go any further afield because we were afraid of further accidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. That is precisely what I wanted to know. So you did not stray from the road?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: At line 62 -- actually, page 62, line 13, you said that your truck took the bodies from Kravica, as well as some other trucks that were there from Milici and other locations. Do you know approximately how many bodies were transferred from Kravica in total?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I said a moment ago that when I was present, there were between 4- and 500 corpses that were buried in the mass grave. If from the school and Konjevic Polje there were, say, 50 or 40, it would mean that the rest, that is to say between 400 and 450, were taken from Kravica to Glogova when I was present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Based on all information available to you, do you know whether there was a total of 400 to 500 people buried from Kravica and that there were 50 from Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I said that it is my estimate that there were buried between 4- and 500 people when I was present. If there were 50 from Konjevic Polje and the school, it would mean that from Kravica that would have been between 400 and 450.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please do not be upset for asking again because you said that it only included your presence. When you were present there were any people buried in the grave?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I said a moment ago that they were. And there were probably more people buried there than those who were buried while I was there, because for most of the time, I was not at the location.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. At the location in Kravica, in addition to the 4- to 500, were there more corpses or was this the total number?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: There were more corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. At page 59, line 4, Ms. Hasan told you that it is the position of the Prosecutor that there was a total of 1.131 corpses in Glogova. In line 7 you said that it sounded like a credible figure.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. I believe there were more people who were buried there while I was absent than there were those who were buried there when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is this: The number of 1.131, was this the total number of people buried there with or without you?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes, I think that is the correct figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. At page 55 to 57 you were asked about the corpses collected from the school compound and taken to Glogova and from Konjevic Polje. Can you recall a total number of corpses that were taken, approximately, from the school-yard in Bratunac and from Konjevic Polje that you saw, and you indicated some locations where you saw them? Can you give us a total?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: In the school-yard of the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac I saw 5 or 6 corpses and I told the driver about them. When he collected them that evening, the next day he told me he had collected more. He told me that the figure I told him was incorrect and that there were more. He picked them all up, and on the day when we were digging at Glogova, he brought them there and they were buried there. When he said there were more, we can guess that there may have been twice as many or let's say between 12 and even up to 18, and then there was a truck-load of corpses from Konjevic Polje, that is to say between 20 and 25. It would all add up to around 40 corpses from Konjevic Polje and along the road between Konjevic Polje and Kravica and Glogova, plus the corpses from the school-yard of the Vuk Karadzic school in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I apologise for repeating this because at page 58, line 17, you said one truck. I was interested in whether 40 corpses could be put on a single truck?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: There was one truck from the school-yard which arrived in Glogova to the location and there was another truck from Konjevic Polje to Glogova, that makes two trucks, which we discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 47, lines 13 onwards, you identified two people who were registered in the hospital log-book. One was wounded and the other dead. Since you know who the persons in question were, let us not mention their names. Without revealing their identity, can you tell us what kind of incident it was that one of the soldiers was killed and the other wounded? And what was the cause of that incident?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I was accompanied by the few men I told you about at the dinner and I was then told that there had been an incident at Sandici in Kravica where a Muslim man managed to seize a weapon from a special unit policeman. He fired at him, killing him. And the other person prevented him from killing anyone else by grabbing the rifle of the automatic -- the barrel of the automatic rifle with his left hand. In the fight that ensued, he managed to take the weapon from him but got his hand and fingers burned. He was then bandaged in the hospital and then came to the restaurant in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: When the summary was read out it was stated that you were also an eye-witness of the Kravica events. Could this have been a cause of the clash between the prisoners and those who guarded them?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: General, if you don't mind repeat the question. I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Since there were no dead people before the moment the rifle was seized by one of the prisoners -- up until that moment there weren't any dead, were there?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I don't think there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did that incident when a policeman was killed serve as a reason for revenge or retaliation between the prisoners and the policeman who guarded them?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I didn't ponder that. I'd rather not provide my opinion. I'm not competent to judge that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate that. In any case, the important thing is that there were no killed people before that moment. Perhaps you can tell us because you were a witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If General Tolimir is going to make that statement, I would like to see where that comes from, that there were no people that were killed before that moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: He is just asking the witness about his knowledge and the witness should answer this question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Hasan, a moment ago the witness said that as far as he knew, there were no murders up to that point in time. I just asked him again. He didn't know whether that was the cause and he said that he didn't think about that before. I simply asked him to confirm what he had stated previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question in a simple term. I don't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will simplify my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In your previous answers you said that there were no killings until the incident when a Muslim prisoner grabbed a rifle from a MUP member.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is, I think, not a correct quotation of the answer of the witness. He said something different. I have to try to find the page. 67. You asked him: "Since there were no dead people before the moment the rifle was seized by one of the prisoners, up until that moment there weren't any dead, were there?" This was your question. And the witness answered: "I don't think there were." This is nothing about killing of people. But you put to him if there were dead bodies. Please repeat your question in a correct way.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you for reminding me. I consider dead people killed, but I'll repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were there any dead bodies or killed persons at Kravica until the moment when the Muslim prisoner grabbed a rifle from a police officer who guarded him and who was then killed by him? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: General, sir, it's much clearer now and I can say that it's possible that people got killed even before that. It was around 6.00 or 7.00 in the evening, possibly even before 6.00, when I drove down the road to Konjevic Polje and saw that incident when the soldier in the camouflage uniform killed those five people. And I don't know when this young man was wounded so I don't know if that triggered the subsequent killings or not. As far as I was able to tell from the medical log-book from Bratunac which says that he was brought there at 1745, which may coincide with the hour when I went there and returned. So that it's clearer now. But I cannot state with certainty whether there were any such incidents or not because I don't know exactly when that killing took place or when that survivor was injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we are running out of time. We need our second break and we will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That part will be redacted and, please, Mr. Tolimir, try to avoid to mention his name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I apologise to the witness and the Prosecution. I will no longer mention the witness's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, on page 42, line 4, the Prosecution, while it was reading out the summary, right after your personal information you -- they say that -- they said that you witnessed an event in Kravica, and they mentioned what you saw next to the co-operative building. And in line 21 of the same page it was mentioned that you were at the Jasen restaurant. Here is my question to you: Did you have the meeting with Mr. Beara, which you mention on page 43, line 12, did you have that meeting before you witnessed that incident?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Before the incident I spent some three to four, maybe five, hours before I met Colonel Beara, because I met him after 9.00 p.m. and I was at Kravica around 5.00 or 6.00, I'm not sure, but it was in the late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us if you can remember the date when it was, I mean the incident at Kravica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: If I had given a statement to that effect in Banja Luka for the first time, I wouldn't remember, but being here, I remember it was the 13th, day after Saint Peter's day. It happened at Kravica and I had dinner with the aforementioned gentlemen at Jasen and after that I was with Mr. Beara. So it was on the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you witnessed that incident and you mention it in your statement, and since you first saw that incident and only had the meeting afterward, does that sentence about the use of your machinery in the future events make sense, shouldn't you have referred to past events? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: What Colonel Beara asked me, and that's what I said too, I did what he ordered me to do. Whether there was any logic in it, I don't think so because I said to him, "What shall we do in another municipality with this small machine and two trucks," and so on. Why he asked me to do that, I don't know, you should ask him. But I carried out the order issued to me. Whether there was any logic in it or not, well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I only wanted to know whether you had seen those shot people before the meeting with Mr. Beara. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there eye-witnesses until the end of the burial of the bodies in the mass grave about which you confirmed the allegations of the Prosecution that 1131 bodies were buried there, so were there any eye-witnesses who stayed there until the end as long as the mass grave was open? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I believe so. And I think that they are still around, some died but I believe that both persons who used those machines, Mr. Simic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Don't mention names. I'm not interested in the names. I'm only interested in whether or not people -- there are any people who stayed until the end and covered that mass grave?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes, I think there are such people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since there are eye-witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I request both speakers to pause between question and answer and the next question. Because you are using the same language, it's quite difficult for the interpreters to get everything right. Please pause between question and answer. Mr. Tolimir, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And I thank the witness for saying that he thinks there are such people who were eye-witnesses. Please tell us now whether, apart from these 50 you mentioned or I don't know which number from Konjevic Polje and the school-yard at Bratunac, any other corpses from Bratunac were buried at Glogova? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge. Except for the school-yard of the Vuk Karadzic school at Bratunac, then Konjevic Polje, then the main road from Konjevic Polje to Bratunac or Glogova, and from Kravica, I don't think any corpses were brought from other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Your people who carried out the sanitation of the places you mentioned, did they transport the entire number of 1131 that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I said as much, but I'll repeat. The men I had at my disposal used one FAP truck and the others drove trucks that were mobilised at Zvornik, Milici and Vlasenica. And your question was whether I and my men did it, no, we didn't. We only transported bodies on one FAP 13 truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. That's exactly what you said during the examination-in-chief. Here is my following question: Were corpses transported from the same location on your FAP and on trucks mobilised from other municipalities? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Talking about the location at Kravica in front of the farming co-operative building, mobilised trucks from Zvornik, Milici and Vlasenica plus this FAP 13 of ours were used to transport corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'm just interested in whether or not it was the same location. Let us take a look at P1033. That's statement of yours that you gave on 13 October 2000. No date is mentioned there. And I'm grateful to you for saying that those events began on the 13th. Now, let me ask you if you know on which date the transportation from that location at Kravica to Glogova began? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry, just one moment. This document shouldn't be broadcast. It is confidential. Now your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transportation of bodies from Kravica to the mass grave at Glogova was on the 14th, which means on the next day after the first incident at Kravica in front of the farming co-operative building.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for this information. On page 5 of this document, P1033, I'm especially interested in what can be found on page 4 in English. The investigator who examined you then, on 13 October 2000, said in line 5 that you are not supposed to speak about the people who were escaping through the forest. Did the utility services from Bratunac or anywhere else collect those killed from the column that tried to break through and transport them to any location that's known to you?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, those who were killed during the break-through, whether or not my people collected those bodies and transported them to the grave-site? Well, in that case my answer is no, we did not collect those corpses because we weren't anywhere near the combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that such bodies were left on the ground where they got killed in combat or otherwise? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Well, you can believe me that there were such cases too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since according to testimonies of witnesses there was a number of corpses along the path used for the break-through of the column in the territory of Bratunac municipality, do you know whether the military ever issued an order to collect those bodies since they were in the territory of the Bratunac municipality? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. We will redact the last answer and your comment. Mr. Tolimir, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Hasan, or Mrs. It was my mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us the following: Pobudjanska Kamenica, is that in the territory of Bratunac municipality?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think that Kamenica is in the Zvornik municipality, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Bare, is that in the territory of Bratunac municipality? Have you heard of such a location, Bare, and is it in the Bratunac municipality?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Well, to tell you honestly, I haven't heard of Bare.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We had a number of witnesses here who testified about a large number of mortal remains at Bare, more than 600, and at Pobudjanska Kamenica, more than 300. Have you heard or do you have any knowledge about whether anybody collected the corpses along the path of the column which went from Srebrenica to Baljkovica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: If we are talking about the company and the civilian protection, I can tell you for sure that nobody ever took part in the collection of dead bodies in those two locations with my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, then, do you have any information or knowledge about whether the representatives of Zvornik municipality, since you think that Pobudjanska Kamenica may be located in that territory, do you have any information whether they collected the executed men along the part of the column from Srebrenica to Baljkovica?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Well, that's a logical thing, isn't it? If Kamenica is in the territory of Zvornik municipality, then it's within their jurisdiction and then its their duty to collect those bodies, but I haven't heard anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Then how can it be possible that some of the people who were killed at those locations were found in the mass graves and identified with the help of DNA? It must mean that somebody did collect those bodies after all.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Well, I'm certainly not going to say that what you are saying is not true, but to say that I know how those bodies ended up in the mass graves together with the people who lost their lives in the area of Bratunac, well, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us what you know. I merely asked you whether you heard something to that effect. On page 7 of the same document that is still on the screen, lines 10 to 12, that's page 7 in English, you said that the workers of the company whose manager you are never carried out either cleaning up or asanacija of any territory or theatre of war outside the communications. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: About which period we are talking? If we are still talking about the same period, it is true that we never collected any bodies outside the communications and we did not carry out any sanitation or asanacija elsewhere. As I just told you, we collected some bodies which were 2 or 3 metres from the communication but not from any other place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Line 12, the same page, 7, you said that you never carried the sanitation or asanacija of Srebrenica. My question is: Can you now state for the record whether the staff of the company whose manager you were, have they ever carried out sanitation or asanacija in the town or municipality of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I don't know how many times I already said that. I claim with full responsibility that the workers of the public utility company did not carry out sanitation or asanacija in Srebrenica. The reason for that is that in Bratunac there were many Serbian inhabitants of Srebrenica. They could hardly wait to go back, and as soon as they went back, they established their own company. They had their own vehicles, dumpsters, and everything else that we had in my company in Bratunac, only they had it much better.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: On pages 9, 10 and 11 of your statement, the investigator who interviewed you asked you on a number of occasions who ordered you to carry out the asanacija of the battle-field. However, you just explain how it went on. So I would like you to state once again for the record, is the public utility service responsible or guilty if it receives an order to bury corpses found in the territory of the municipality at a certain location? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I think that the public utility service has no responsibility whatsoever. The reason for that is as follows: During the war, we used to receive orders both from the civilian authorities and the military authorities and we had a duty to carry out those orders. That is why I think that the public utility service has no responsibility in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you that because you were cautioned here and I simply want it to be known that you did what people who were your superiors ordered you to do; is that true?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here on page 11, perhaps because you didn't have specific information about the chronology, you stated that you saw Beara on Tuesday, 11th of July. Is it maybe a misprint or you couldn't remember it properly or is it maybe a misunderstanding? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: That's the statement from the year 2000 given in Banja Luka, isn't it? When we talk about Banja Luka, I already said that during my previous testimony before this honourable court, I said that I made many mistakes about the dates on that occasion. The reason for that is that Mr. Ruez was giving me dates and I was merely confirming them. However, later on, when I saw that Saint Peter's day was on the 12th, that something, for instance, in Kravica went on on the 13th, that's when I realised that many of those dates were completely false. I don't know whether Mr. Ruez did it on purpose, but he was the one saying out the dates and I was confirming them. So I'm not sure that this statement that I gave in Banja Luka is accurate when it comes to dates and chronology.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you very much for what you just said. Now, take a look at line 21 and 22. That's page 10 in English. This is where you speak about the 11th or the 10th. So does that mean that it couldn't have been the way that it was described here in the transcript of your interview?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: General, I didn't understand you well. What statement are you talking about now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. It's the statement under the number 1033. Take a look at lines 21 and 22. You have it in front of you. I want page 11 to be shown to you. It's line 22 on page 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which page and line in English?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's line 9 in English. You can see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Maybe so that you can connect those things, take a look at line 17 in Serbian, when Ruez asked you: "Tell me, since you said that Colonel Beara said that this operation was planned, do I conclude that this contact was just prior to the fall of the enclave?" Answer: "Day before, just the day before they planned to take over Srebrenica." Then he says: "Okay, so I don't know if you have a perfect memory of these dates because it was a long time ago, but the fall was on Tuesday, the 11th of July. Would it then be Monday, the 10th, that Colonel Beara went to see you and made this request?" And you say: "I don't recall ..." So my question is, bearing in mind everything that you said, that you were relying on the dates that he provided to you and the chronology that he provided, does that mean that you simply confirmed the dates that you heard and that it could not have occurred on the 10th or the 11th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think you should put it in a complete manner to the witness. In line 11 in the English version, it reads: "I cannot recall the exact date, but that was the day prior to the fall of Srebrenica, so that would be then." He didn't answer simply, "I don't recall." That would be the complete quotation. Now, sir, please, if you are able to do that, answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I already stated, during this testimony as well as my previous testimony, that I met Mr. Beara the day after Saint Peter's day, so that's the 13th. Here I can now see that Mr. Ruez was talking about the 11th, saying was it on the 11th or maybe on the 10th, before the fall of Srebrenica. Now, I'm not quite sure when exactly Srebrenica fell, but I have to say that I had the first meeting with Colonel Beara on the 13th after 9.00 in the evening. The second meeting was during that same night around 1.00 or 1.30 a.m. And that's the truth. I also asked during my previous testimony that I wouldn't like to go back all the time to those dates that I mentioned in my interview in Banja Luka with Mr. Ruez because you can see it quite clearly that many of those dates are inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. That's exactly what I wanted to see. I wanted to clarify those things which were still not clear. Everything else that was also not clear in Mr. Ruez's questions, now you have the chance to address all those ambiguities and all the things that were not clear to Mr. Ruez. So that's the reason why I'm not going to ask you anything about that anymore. So am I right if I say that the first burials at Glogova began on the 14th, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that the victims for the first burials must have originated before the 14th?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: Before and on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 22 of your statement, the investigator asked you whether you remember the buses in Bratunac. It's page 19 in English. Lines 1 to 17, you talk about it on the whole page. And you said that you remembered. And at line 22 -- page 22, line 16 to 17 -- excuse me, page 22, line 16 to 17, you said: "Yes, I remember that, but the second day." Now, please, tell us the following: Which buses were you referring to and were those buses full or empty?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I'll try to answer although the question isn't very clear to me. The first buses I saw were in front of the Bratunac Municipal Assembly building. I was there with Srbislav Davidovic, providing water with the people on the buses. They were thirsty. The other buses I saw were en route to Konjevic Polje. The next day when I saw the incident in Kravica, that is when I saw both buses and trucks full of women, children, and the elderly, that's what I could see through the windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Since you saw women, children, and the elderly on the buses, can you tell us, if you remember, whether they were transferred to Kladanj, to ABiH territory, or did they end up in a different place?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: While I was in Kravica and when I turned back in Konjevic Polje, at the check-point in Konjevic Polje certain buses were stopped and then released one by one. I don't know how far they went, though. I know for certain that while I was in Konjevic Polje for that brief period of time, that no one was taken off those buses or trucks and that they took the road to Milici. I can't tell you how far they got, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to clarify for the transcript something that was unclear from your interview. On page 33 and 34, which is also page 30 in the English, lines 33 and 34. It's page 30 in the English. In line 20 -- sorry, 21, you were asked: "What is it that you can recall about your movements on the 14th of July?" When we look up, you were asked by Mr. Ruez about the mass grave. My question is this: Do you recall when the mass graves in Glogova were covered finally and when the people engaged in digging them stopped working?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: As for the people I had at my disposal, we worked there for three or four days. However, the work was continued later on and I found out that there was some work all the way up to the 19th. It was difficult to believe because I just couldn't fathom that so much time would be needed up there. In any case, I know that I withdrew my personnel after three or four days. As for the other piece of information, that is something I learned from people in Bratunac with whom I communicated, from the military and others. They told me that there was work to be done until the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You managed to answer some of my following questions about the time until which there was work around the mass graves. Do you know whether those graves were later on opened again after the 19th? Was anything done with them? Were the corpses taken away? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: PW-064
utterances.text: I heard some things and some I saw for myself. I know that those mass graves such as the one from 1992 which was some 1 or 1 and a half kilometres away from the Drina bridge in Bratunac downstream, as well as the Glogova grave, I say the grave but actually there were three smaller and one bigger mass grave there in the same location. In any case, as for all those graves, it was Mr. Nikolic with the assistance of the army, were dug out and the bodies transferred to different parts of the municipality of Srebrenica. On two or three occasions, I also saw trucks going through Bratunac en route to Srebrenica that were full of corpses. People were saying that Momir Nikolic was in charge of it, that he was transferring corpses from Bratunac to the territory of the municipality of Srebrenica. That is all I can tell you about the transfer of, as Mr. Ruez put it, stolen corpses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you this because the Prosecutor asked you about it on page 36, line 14, and you provided the same answer then as you did now in lines 14 and 15. Thank you. Thank you for having come to testify and for everything that you have said. We'll see through some other witnesses what happened with the corpses referred to by the witnesses at Pobudjanska Kamenica and Bare mentioned by Mr. Ruez. Thank you, again. May god bless you. Have a safe journey back from The Hague to your final destination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this will be all the Defence has for the witness. We have no further questions of him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Hasan, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, you will be pleased to hear that this concludes your examination in this trial. You are now free to return to your normal activities, your usual life. The Chamber would like to thank you that you were able to come to The Hague and to provide us with your knowledge. Thank you very much again. We adjourn and resume next Monday, 3rd of May, in Courtroom I at 2 -- sorry, I made a mistake. It's the 2nd of May in Courtroom I at 2.15 in the afternoon. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 2nd day of May, 2011, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
